systems.name: Lantern
systems.survey_history: Repeatedly visited by Lastlight survey crews; navigation solution considered dependable.

bodies.name: Lantern b
bodies.summary: Hot inner rock with little commercial interest.

bodies.name: Lantern c
bodies.summary: Thin atmosphere, extensive subsurface water ice and broad equatorial flats suitable for temporary expedition bases.

bodies.name: Lantern Outer Belt
bodies.summary: Sparse belt with useful volatiles but mediocre metal concentrations.

systems.commercial_outlook: Useful primarily as a logistics stepping stone. Water makes local propellant production plausible, but no major export justifies permanent settlement yet.

systems.name: Morrow
systems.survey_history: Extensively surveyed after an atmospheric biosignature attracted scientific funding.

bodies.name: Morrow b
bodies.summary: Temperate world with microbial and simple multicellular native life concentrated in shallow inland seas.
bodies.special: Landing zones are tightly controlled to avoid contamination.

bodies.name: Morrow c
bodies.summary: Airless mineral-poor moon used as a clean staging location for biological expeditions.

systems.commercial_outlook: Scientifically important but deliberately difficult to exploit. Most freight is sterile equipment, laboratories, consumables and sample-return hardware.

systems.name: Pilgrim
systems.survey_history: Mapped early because its compact planetary system made a cheap survey target.

bodies.name: Pilgrim c
bodies.summary: Water-rich but otherwise ordinary frozen world.

systems.commercial_outlook: A disappointment. Everything Pilgrim contains is available closer to established markets. It survives on charts mostly because it is a useful navigation reference.

systems.name: Cairn
systems.survey_history: Two major surveys and several commercial prospecting visits disagree about the value of the outer system.

bodies.name: Cairn b
bodies.summary: High-gravity dry planet with dense atmosphere and severe surface winds.

bodies.name: Cairn Outer System
bodies.summary: Remote observations suggest several icy bodies and a debris concentration; orbital solutions remain incomplete.

systems.commercial_outlook: Interesting enough to revisit, not proven enough to finance a colony. A classic speculative survey destination.

systems.name: Needle
systems.survey_history: Named for the narrow safe approach geometry identified during the first crewed survey.

bodies.name: Needle Debris Plane
bodies.summary: A broad debris structure complicates high-speed navigation but contains accessible nickel-iron bodies.

systems.commercial_outlook: Potentially profitable extraction, but insurers and carriers dislike the navigation risk. Specialized operators may find opportunity here.

systems.name: Harbor
systems.survey_history: A remote survey identified an unusually benign outer moon, prompting its optimistic name. Only one crewed expedition has reached it.

bodies.name: Harbor Giant
bodies.summary: Large gas giant with a complex moon system.

bodies.name: Harbor
bodies.summary: Subsurface ocean moon with accessible surface ice, useful volatiles and low radiation compared with neighboring moons.

systems.commercial_outlook: One of the better candidates for a permanent outward logistics depot, but current traffic does not justify the investment.

systems.name: Redoubt
systems.survey_history: Cataloged remotely. No confirmed crewed entry.
systems.commercial_outlook: Unknown. Long-range observations suggest multiple rocky planets, but published data is insufficient for commercial planning.

systems.name: Vesper
systems.survey_history: Known from remote astronomy and automated observations. No dependable local navigation solution.
systems.commercial_outlook: No demonstrated economic value. Its position makes it interesting as a possible extension of the outward corridor.

systems.name: Faraday
systems.survey_history: Remote observations show frequent stellar activity. No crewed survey has been funded.
systems.commercial_outlook: Probably hostile to conventional settlement; still of interest to stellar researchers and specialized survey crews.

systems.name: Blackglass
systems.survey_history: One commercial survey returned unusually promising spectroscopy from a dark inner asteroid family before funding collapsed.

bodies.name: Blackglass Family
bodies.summary: Very dark carbonaceous bodies with unusual trace-element signatures.

systems.commercial_outlook: Potentially valuable, potentially a costly false positive. Survey data is privately traded and inconsistent.

systems.name: Holloway
systems.survey_history: Detected and characterized remotely; currently beyond routine commercial support.
systems.commercial_outlook: Unknown. Listed in expedition planning software mostly because it is the next obvious target beyond Redoubt.

systems.name: Sable
systems.commercial_outlook: No established commercial case. It represents the practical edge of what most public charts bother naming.
